divergence.subject: experiments/sol_root_matched_config/.cart0/700.100.RECEIPT.json (v0.2 continuation packet receipt)
divergence.root_cause: the committed receipt embeds machine-local absolute paths (D:\Projects\Tier-Bench\worktrees\luna-sol-anchor-replication-v2\...) in checks[].detail for exists:* checks; verify_continuation.py's receipt_matches_subjects performs deep equality on the full receipt dict, so the check can only pass on the machine and directory where the receipt was built
divergence.evidence: all seven subject_sha256 values and verifier_sha256 recomputed in this environment MATCH the committed receipt; only the environment-dependent detail strings differ
divergence.classification: portability defect in the v0.2 receipt format, not a content divergence; the v0.3 artifacts under custody fully reproduce
divergence.note: the prior local claude verification passed this check because it ran on the same machine and worktree path where the receipt was built; same-machine verification structurally cannot detect this defect class. This is the failure mode the cross-machine custody layer exists to catch, and it is the same defect class the paired review had already identified in prose (machine-local paths are cache addresses, not scientific addresses).
divergence.suggested_remedy: additive, for the successor packet already agreed (schema-versioned 000.000.json): store repo-relative paths in check details, or exclude environment-dependent details from the receipt_matches_subjects comparison as is already done for receipt_size_limit; requires separate authorization

state_assertion.reason: verification of the v0.3 custody subject reproduced fully, but the run surfaced a deterministic cross-machine failure in the committed v0.2 continuation receipt; per protocol a divergence is preserved and cannot close the gate by itself. Disposition of whether this blocks cross_engine_verified_unmerged for the v0.3 subject (whose own artifacts reproduced) belongs to the operator.
